name: Brennerpass
kurzbeschreibung: The storied Brenner Pass (1,370 m) links North and South Tyrol: historic Roman crossing, outlet shopping, scenic cycle path, and key transport artery.
beschreibung:
Overview

The historic Brenner Pass sits at an elevation of 1,370 meters above sea level and represents the topographically lowest and most accessible mountain pass across the entire main alpine ridge of the Central Alps. It marks the long-standing international border between the Austrian province of Tyrol and the autonomous province of South Tyrol in Italy. Nestled between the Stubai and Zillertal Alps, the pass has served for millennia as Europe's most vital north-south transit corridor connecting Central Europe with the Mediterranean. In antiquity, the Romans upgraded the ancient pack mule trail into the paved military road Via Raetia. During the Middle Ages, German kings and Holy Roman emperors travelled across the Brenner along the Via Imperii to be crowned in Rome. Today, the route links the scenic B182 highway, the A13 Brenner motorway, and Carl von Etzel's historic Brenner railway, while the landmark Brenner Base Tunnel project is currently underway beneath the mountains.

Route & Requirements

Exploring the pass summit requires no alpine conditioning and is ideal as a fascinating travel stopover or as a starting point for leisure cyclists and sightseers. On the Austrian side, federal road B182 climbs gently through the Wipptal valley via scenic curves to the pass crest, home to the international Brenner railway station and the Designer Outlet Brenner. Both facilities are completely barrier-free and step-free. For cyclists, the Brenner Pass is a classic jumping-off point: the 96-kilometer paved Eisacktal cycle path begins right at the summit, following a disused railway line on a gentle downhill gradient through Sterzing and Brixen all the way to Bolzano. Because weather can change rapidly at alpine passes, carrying windproof clothing is recommended.

Visit & Arrival

The mountain pass and its road links are open 24/7 year-round. On the Austrian side, the federal highway B182 is completely toll-free, while the A13 motorway is subject to a distance-based toll. Public transport connections are exceptional: line S3 of the Tyrolean S-Bahn runs every half hour from Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof directly to Brenner station (travel time approx. 35 minutes), and international Eurocity trains call here regularly. Motorists reach the pass summit either via the toll motorway A13 (exit Brennersee) or toll-free along the scenic B182.

Tips

Visit the symbolic border church of Maria am Wege, built in 1962, featuring expressive modernist stained glass windows. The Designer Outlet Brenner, offering over 70 boutique shops and cafes, is open daily and invites travellers to browse and take a relaxed break.
preis: Pass summit and federal road B182 free of charge (A13 motorway toll applies)
